App terms of use

These terms explain what the Stuck Not Broken app is, how subscriptions work, and what is expected at live events.

Last updated: November 1, 2026

Who runs the app

The Stuck Not Broken app is run by Justin Sunseri, a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist in California, as a sole proprietor at 924 N Yosemite Ave, Stockton, CA 95203. You can reach him at justin@stucknotbroken.com.

What this is

Stuck Not Broken is a tool for noticing your experience through the lens of the nervous system and practicing your way back to safety. It is for education and self-practice. It is not therapy, medical care or diagnosis, and it does not replace any of them. Using the app, joining a live event or writing to Justin does not make him your therapist or create any client relationship.

In a crisis

If you are in danger or thinking about harming yourself, call or text 988 in the US to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, or call your local emergency number. The app and its live events cannot respond to an emergency.

Use it your way

Everyone is different. There is no failing here and no streak to keep. You can use the app when you want and practice at your own pace.

Who can use it

You need to be 18 or older to make an account. You are responsible for keeping your sign-in to yourself and for what happens under your account.

Subscriptions

The price and length of each plan are shown before you subscribe. Paid plans renew automatically until you cancel.

If you subscribe in the iPhone app, payment is charged to your Apple ID when you confirm the purchase. Your subscription renews automatically unless you cancel it at least 24 hours before the end of the current period, and your Apple ID is charged for the renewal within the 24 hours before the period ends. You can manage or cancel your subscription in iPhone Settings by tapping your name and then Subscriptions.

If you subscribe on the website, Stripe handles payment, and you can cancel in the app under Settings, then Your plan, then Manage, change, or cancel subscription.

When you cancel, you keep access until the end of the period you already paid for. Then your account moves to the free plan, and your check-ins, journal and history stay.

If a price changes, you will hear about it before your next renewal, and you can cancel before the new price applies.

Refunds

Subscriptions are not refunded, except where the law requires it. Apple decides refunds for purchases made in the iPhone app, and you can request one at reportaproblem.apple.com.

Apple's license

If you got the app from the App Store, Apple's standard license agreement for App Store apps also applies.

Content

The practices, recordings, articles, videos and sheets in the app are Justin's work. You can use them for your own practice. You cannot copy, resell, publish or share paid content outside your account.

What you write

Your check-ins, notes and journal entries belong to you. They are stored so the app can show them back to you, as the app privacy policy explains.

Live events and community spaces

Justin hosts live events where he teaches and guides practice. Live events can change or be canceled. Events that are recorded for replay are marked ahead of time, and your camera, mic and chat are always optional.

Everyone at a live event or in the community spaces is asked to follow these guidelines:

  • Be kind. You can disagree, but do not bully, target or attack anyone.
  • Respect each other's privacy. What others share stays with the group, so do not record, screenshot or pass on other members' names, faces or words.
  • Do not share the details of traumatic experiences, your own or anyone else's. They can be hard for others to hear. This is not a therapeutic setting, and those details are better brought to your own therapist.
  • Do not sell, spam or message members about your own services or products.
  • Be careful recommending outside programs or methods, and do not endorse medicines, diets or other physical wellness options.
  • Do not promote political, religious or other groups. Sharing your own experience is welcome.

If the guidelines are not followed

Justin or a moderator decides when a guideline has been broken. Depending on what happened, they may remove a message, warn you publicly or privately, or remove you from a live event. For serious or repeated problems, they may remove your access to live events and the community spaces, or close your account. Removal does not come with a refund, including any unused part of a paid period.

When Justin shares something from the community

Justin may use things shared in the community or at live events in his podcast, videos or writing. He puts members' privacy first. He anonymizes what he shares, and he asks your permission before using your words, voice or image.

No guarantee

Justin works to keep the app running and its content accurate, but he cannot promise it will always be available, free of errors, or that it will change how you feel. To the extent the law allows, his liability is limited to what you paid in the 12 months before a claim, or $100, whichever is more.

Governing law

These terms are governed by the laws of the State of California. Any dispute goes to the state or federal courts in San Joaquin County, California, except that either side can use small claims court.

Changes

Justin will update the app and these terms over time. When the terms change in a way that matters, you will hear about it in the app or by email at least 30 days before the change applies.
